stem:
Alok fills $\dfrac{1}{5}$ of a tank in one hour. Kavya fills $\dfrac{1}{10}$ of the same tank in one hour. They work together on that tank.

Which claim correctly combines their work?

options.text: Together they fill $\dfrac{1}{5}+\dfrac{1}{10}=\dfrac{3}{10}$ of the tank each hour, so one full tank takes $\dfrac{10}{3}$ hours.
Call the answer the phrase individual rate alone, and stop.
The time for one full tank produces their separate hourly rates, so Alok starts from $\dfrac{10}{3}$ hours instead of adding rates.
Combine the rates by the inverse-proportion constant $xy=k$ used for speed–time pairs, instead of adding the hourly shares of the tank.

teacher.key_rationale: Add hourly shares 1/5+1/10=3/10, then time for one tank is 10/3 hours. Naming individual rate alone, reversing time into rates, or swapping in inverse-proportion all miss combining shared work by adding rates.
